correctness.rationale: With Haar probability, degree ℓ contributes (2ℓ+1) times its character to the projection kernel, and the kernel of the data operator TT* is its restriction in both arguments. For half-turns with axes u,v the character is U_{2ℓ}(u·v); the Chebyshev sum/derivative yields C^{(2)}_{2L−2}. Probability-normalized Funk–Hecke on S² contributes the factor 1/2 in the integral, with only even degrees descending to the quotient. Integration by parts gives each successive level difference as a positive constant times ∫sin(2Lθ)P_{2j+1}(cos θ)dθ. The Legendre cosine coefficients are positive by the generating function, and each odd frequency k in its support satisfies |k|<2L and contributes 4L/(4L²−k²)>0. The constant level is L by the U-polynomial boundary values, and the lowest level follows from the leading coefficient and Legendre norm, so all displayed levels are positive, including L=1 where the lone level is 1. The rank, nullity, reconstruction on the orthogonal complement and condition number then follow by spectral decomposition and the central binomial asymptotic. Independent exact rational computation for L=1–8 checked strict order, endpoints, trace and dimensions, e.g. (2,8/5) and (3,96/35,128/63). Replay: generate Gegenbauer and Legendre polynomials by their three-term recurrences and apply the exact moment functional t^(2r)→1/(2r+1), t^(2r+1)→0 to their products. This corroborates finite bandwidths; the analytic argument supplies all bandwidths.

evidence: Dai–Xu (2.8) gives the degree-r projection kernel (r+α)C_r^{(α)}(x·y)/α, α=(d−2)/2 on S^{d−1}.
DLMF 18.18.16 gives the full connection expansion from C_n^{(μ)} to C_{n−2s}^{(α)} with coefficient [(α+n−2s)/α](μ)_{n−s}(μ−α)_s/[(α+1)_{n−s}s!], and cites Andrews et al. (1999), Theorem 7.1.4′.
broader_coverage.reasoning: For S³, α=1. Summing the even addition kernels to degree 2L−2 telescopes to C_{2L−2}^{(2)} using C_r^{(2)}−C_{r−2}^{(2)}=(r+1)C_r^{(1)}, which follows directly from the generating functions. On S², the target projectors are (2h+1)P_h. Consequently the coefficients of the restricted kernel in that normalized projector basis are exactly the general connection coefficients with the factor 2h+1 removed.

evidence: Put m=L−1, s=m−j, t=m+j. Substituting n=2m, μ=2, α=1/2 into the connection formula and dividing the P_{2j} coefficient by 4j+1 gives λ_{L,j}=(3/2)_s(2)_t/[s!(3/2)_t].

For j<m, the adjacent ratio is [s/(s+1/2)]·[(t+2)/(t+3/2)]<1 precisely because s<t+3/2. All levels are positive. At j=0 the Pochhammer factors cancel to (2)_m/m!=L; at j=m the level is (2)_{2m}/(3/2)_{2m}=(2m+1)2^{4m}/[(4m+1)binom(4m,2m)].
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: This classical product formula already gives the full ordered spectrum and both endpoints by cancellation. Summing 4j+1 and subtracting from the band dimension gives rank and kernel dimension. Taking the square root of the endpoint ratio and applying the central binomial asymptotic gives the stated condition law. The minimum-norm inversion is the standard pseudoinverse on those projector spaces. No additional spectral lemma is required to derive the frozen result.

evidence: Bernstein–Pesenson identify SO(3) with S³/{±1}; their Radon operator, however, integrates over subgroup fibers.

With a unit quaternion written (cos(θ/2),u sin(θ/2)), half-turns have scalar part zero and correspond to the equatorial S² modulo antipodes. The degree-ℓ Wigner projector pulled up to S³ has zonal kernel (2ℓ+1)U_{2ℓ}(q·r), which is exactly the S³ degree-2ℓ addition kernel.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Thus the frozen operator is equatorial restriction of the even spherical band with probability norms; Haar probability pushes forward from the uniform sphere and the equatorial probability measure pushes forward to RP². It is not any of the inspected fiber-average operators.

originality.rationale: The exact levels, strict order, rank and asymptotic are a mechanical specialization of the spherical harmonic addition and Funk–Hecke formulas and the classical Gegenbauer connection formula. A direct prior article using the half-turn trace terminology was not established; the failure is the explicit broader-formula implication, not an assertion that a cited fiber transform or torus trace has the same spectrum.
residual_risks: The bounded search did not establish whether a prior paper explicitly states the operator under half-turn or equatorial-trace terminology. The mathematical implication from standard formulas does not depend on resolving that bibliographic question.
